title: The viral ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ vs. ‘GTA V’ trend, but make it Philly sports: Baby Sixers, end of an era, and more - Inquirer.com
content: Fans online are noting how much the world has changed in the 13 years between the debut of “GTA V” and this week’s highly anticipated “GTA VI” release. The city’s sports scene and its current athletes are no exception. Thursday will mark the release of one of the most highly-anticipated video games in years, Grand Theft Auto VI. The video game franchise has had a massive cultural impact across different platforms, spreading from the video game world into the sports sphere — partnering with sports teams like the Miami Heat for themed game nights with “Vice City” jerseys, and leaving athletes like Steven Adams worried about players’ performance across the NBA and NFL once the game is released. Its return ends a 13-year wait since the release of GTA V, which came out in September 2013. A lot has changed since. When it debuted, Barack Obama was president; the second film in The Hunger Games series, Catching Fire, was about to be released in theaters; Breaking Bad was airing its final episodes; and Katy Perry’s “Roar” was on repeat on the radio stations. As different as it sounds, that’s nothing compared with the changes that have happened in Philly sports — we’re still making Hunger Games movies, after all. In fact, 2013 itself was a big year of change across the city’s sports scene. As fans all over the internet celebrate the game’s long-awaited release by comparing life 13 years apart, let’s take a look at the viral trend through the lens of Philly sports. » READ MORE: Two Temple football teammates had different ‘Love Is Blind’ experiences. Their time in Philly helped them navigate it. The current Sixers roster includes future Hall of Famer LeBron James, five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown, two-time All-Star Tyrese Maxey, former league MVP Joel Embiid, and rising star VJ Edgecombe. But 13 years ago, during the release of GTA V, these players were all at very different stages of their lives and basketball careers. James was on the verge of winning his second NBA title with the Miami Heat and already had close to a decade of NBA experience. Embiid, meanwhile, was a freshman at the University of Kansas, and had only been playing basketball for a couple of years. Brown was a junior at Wheeler High School in Georgia. Maxey (13 years old) and Edgecombe (8) were still dreaming of playing at the next level. The current 76ers starting five when GTA V came out is CRAZY 😂 pic.twitter.com/UJtPwPrx8f The Sixers’ organization was also at a different stage of its life. In 2013, the team was at the start of The Process under former general manager Sam Hinkie. The multiyear rebuilding strategy focused on exchanging current players for assets, and intentionally losing to gain multiple high draft picks. Some of the first dominoes fell when the team traded reigning All-Star and future six-time All-Defensive Team player Jrue Holiday to the New Orleans Pelicans on draft night in 2013 for the rights to Nerlens Noel and a future first-round pick. With the 11th overall pick, they also selected Michael Carter-Williams, who would be traded away less than 18 months later — after winning rookie of the year. » READ MORE: Fans show appreciation to Tyrese Maxey, who hosted his fifth annual holiday turkey giveaway The Sixers won just 47 games over the next three seasons — including going 19-63 in 2013-14 — resulting in several high draft picks. During The Process, the team selected Embiid with the third-overall pick in the 2014 draft and Jahlil Okafor third overall the following year. Then, with back-to-back first-overall picks in 2016 and 2017, the Sixers took Ben Simmons and Markelle Fultz, respectively. Embiid is the only player from that era who remains on the team, which otherwise looks nothing like the one that is currently off to one of the best starts in the NBA. It was the start of the Chip Kelly era for the Birds. In 2013, following a disappointing 4-12 season that would be head coach Andy Reid’s last with the Eagles, the team hired Kelly, and left fans dreaming of a potentially revolutionary offense under the former Oregon Ducks coach. In Kelly’s first year, he led the Eagles to an NFC East division title with a 10-6 record before losing to the New Orleans Saints in the wild-card round. The 2013 team featured players like Michael Vick, Nick Foles, LeSean McCoy, DeSean Jackson, Zach Ertz, Brandon Graham, Jason Kelce, Connor Barwin, Brent Celek, Fletcher Cox, and DeMeco Ryans. » READ MORE: South Philly 12-year-old says goodbye to part of his ‘53-man dad squad’ in viral video to Jordan Davis But perhaps the biggest difference for Eagles fans in 2013? No Super Bowls. That’s no longer the case, thanks in large part to the contributions of many of the players listed above. The Kelly Era was short-lived. In 2015, during his third season at the helm, Kelly was fired following a 6-9 start. Kelly was criticized for his lack of “emotional intelligence,” as well as for making questionable roster moves that included releasing Jackson, and trading McCoy and Foles. This came after a power struggle that saw him wrestle roster control away from general manager Howie Roseman. Both Jackson and McCoy talked about their time with Kelly on their podcast, The 25/10 Show. But even at their lowest under Kelly, the Eagles had never lost seven straight games — and never had a record this poor, this late in the season. Ahead of the release of GTA VI, the Eagles are 2-7, are in last place in the NFC East, and haven’t won a game since mid-September. Many of the team’s current stars weren’t even in college yet  when GTA V first hit the shelves. And some weren’t even old enough to play the violent game, which carries a “Mature” rating and is meant for players 17 and older. Jalen Hurts was a quarterback at Channelview High School in Texas, Saquon Barkley was a running back at Whitehall High School in Pennsylvania, and Cooper DeJean was just a 10-year-old kid in Odebolt, Iowa. In the years leading up to the 2013 season, the Phillies found plenty of success, but were backsliding each year. During their run of winning five straight National League East titles (2007-2011), the team peaked with a 2008 World Series title, but was eliminated one round earlier each year, capped off by a National League Division Series loss following a 102-win season in 2011. In 2012, the team’s string of playoff appearances and division titles came to an end as they finished the season .500 (81-81), starting a run of nine straight seasons without a winning record and a decade of being shut out of the playoffs. The 2013 team featured household names like Chase Utley, Jimmy Rollins, Cole Hamels, Ryan Howard, Roy Halladay, Cliff Lee, and Carlos Ruiz. But over the next three seasons, almost all of those players would be gone. And in August of that season, with the team at 53-67, manager Charlie Manuel, who led the team to its first title in 28 years, was fired and replaced by Ryne Sandberg, who finished the season as interim manager before taking the role full-time. Roy Halladay SPThe Phillies beat the Marlins 6-4! pic.twitter.com/iUF1rTAeJe The Flyers had made the playoffs in 16 of the previous 17 seasons, but coming off a shortened 2012-13 season (due to the NHL lockout) in which they failed to reach the postseason, they wasted no time acting. The team opened the 2013-14 season with three straight losses, leading to the firing of head coach Peter Laviolette less than a week into the season. Craig Berube stepped in and lead the team to a 42-30-10 record, getting the Flyers back to the playoffs as the third seed in the Metropolitan Division, before they lost to the New York Rangers in the first round. The team featured players like Claude Giroux, Wayne Simmonds, Scott Hartnell, Jakub Voracek, Kimmo Timonen, Steve Mason, and Brayden and Luke Schenn. It also featured one player who is still wearing the orange and black: current Flyers captain and the longest tenured athlete in Philly sports Sean Couturier. Then a 21-year-old center, Couturier was the youngest player on the team — he is now the second oldest at 34 — and was eighth in total points with 39 (13 goals, 26 assists) while appearing in all 82 games. » READ MORE: Jeffrey Lurie needs to address the Eagles’ mess like Dan Hilferty addressed Flyers’ woes In 2013, the Union was in only its fourth year of existence, and was in search of its second Major League Soccer postseason berth, which wouldn’t come for a few more years (2016). Now, 13 years later, the team is a regular in the postseason, qualifying this season for the ninth time in the last 10 years. After a slow start, the team caught fire following the World Cup break, and went several months without losing a game. A few days after the release of GTA VI, the No. 6 seed Union will face the third-seeded New England Revolution in Game 1 of their best-of-three first-round series. The Union’s turnaround has been in part sparked by a trio of young players who was more than just too young to play GTA V; they were likely too young to play most video games: Cavan Sullivan, now 17, was just three when the game was released. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Neil Pierre was six and 20-year-old Frankie Westfield, was seven. Perhaps some of the older players, like Andre Blake, who was drafted by the Union four months after the game’s release, and Alejandro Bedoya, who was already 25 when the game came out, can explain it to them.
